implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the pattern into a delegated property: `val config: Config by lazy { Config.load() }` runs the initialiser on first access under LazyThreadSafetyMode.SYNCHRONIZED (the default, which locks so only one thread initialises and every reader sees the published value), `lazy(LazyThreadSafetyMode.PUBLICATION)` permits concurrent initialiser runs with only one published value when the builder is side-effect free, and NONE drops synchronisation entirely. A companion-object `val` or a top-level `val` is likewise initialised once under the JVM's class-initialisation lock, so the accessor contains no check at all. The hand-written volatile-plus-synchronized double check stays justified only for per-instance state that must be reset, or where the extra Lazy object allocated per instance is measurable.
pitfalls: `by lazy` is per instance: on a class with millions of short-lived instances the delegate object and its lock state cost memory and indirection, while a companion-object val is allocated once.

PUBLICATION can run the initialiser several times concurrently, so it is only correct for side-effect-free builders; NONE is only safe under external confinement such as a single-threaded dispatcher or an actor.
Recursive access from inside the initialiser blocks forever under SYNCHRONIZED (the delegate is reentrant per thread only after publication), so cycles must be broken explicitly.
A `by lazy` property serialises first access across all threads that need it: a slow builder delays every reader, which is often mistaken for a lock-contention problem.
